To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Granger causailty is not able to distinguish mixed noise from truly interacting systems if the noise is not mixed, and PSI is not able to detect non-linear interactions.

PSI is a robust measure of causality that works in the presence of instantaneous mixture of signals with arbitrary spectral content and that Granger causuality fails to distinguish between truly interacting systems and systems with mixed noise if the memory time of the sender is long compared to transmission time of the signal.
Granger causation and PSI are both able to distinguish interacting systems from mixed independent sources, but that Granger causations, but not PSI, is sensitive to non-mixed noise.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to distinguish between truly interacting signals and signals which are only correlated due to mixing of independent sources.
the problem of how to distinguish true information transfer from spurious correlations in the context of mixed noise.
the problem of detecting causal interactions from time series of two interacting signals and we propose the Phase Slope Index as an efficient and robust method for this problem.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PSI is a more robust method for estimating causal interactions between two signals than Granger causality.
PSI is the more robust method to estimate causal interactions in linear systems, whereas Granger causality is more suitable in systems with strong nonlinear interactions.
PSI is a more reliable method to detect causal interactions than Granger Causaility.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PSI is a robust and reliable measure for the detection of linear interactions, whereas Granger causality is not.

PSI is a robust method to estimate causal interactions in linear and nonlinear systems, whereas Granger Causailty is not able to do so in the presence of mixed noise and non-mixed noise with long memory-time of the information sender.
Granger causation, as well as the Phase Slope Index are useful tools for the analysis of interactions between neural populations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Granger Causaility and PSI are not equivalent measures and, therefore, should be used carefully and only in the context of the specific problem at hand.
, in the presence of mixed and non-mixed noise and/or nonlinear interactions, PSI is a better method to detect causal interactions than Granger causality.

, in contrast with the widespread belief that Granger Causaility is a general measure of causal interactions, it is not robust with respect to mixed noise, and that it fails for non-linear interactions.
